title: Early Warning Systems for Better Management of Flash Floods
what_it_is: Early Warning Systems for Better Management of Flash Floods

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on flash floods
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources about spot checks, flood early warnings, penalties for errant contractors, and inter-agency work to reduce flash floods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the Ministry conducts regular spot checks for works which undermine the capacity of the public drainage system to deal with floods; (b) whether there is an effective system that triggers early warnings about flood threats that particular works can pose; and (c) whether the penalties to deal with errant contractors are on par with the severity of the potential damage from the resultant flooding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources in light of recent flash floods across the island and global climate change, whether the Ministry will work with other agencies to reduce incidents of flash floods in key areas of Singapore.

sections.label: PUB drainage design standards
sections.summary: Since 2011, PUB has raised drainage design standards for new developments and redevelopments, increasing their drainage systems' capacity by up to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Since 2011, PUB has raised drainage design standards for new developments and redevelopments, which would increase their drainage systems' capacity by up to 50%.

sections.label: Fines for unauthorised drainage works
sections.summary: A person found guilty may be fined up to $50,000 for unauthorised works affecting the public drainage system and up to $20,000 for unauthorised alteration or interference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Any person found guilty may be fined up to $50,000 for unauthorised works affecting the public drainage system and up to $20,000 for unauthorised alteration or interference to the public drainage system.

sections.label: Reduction in flood-prone areas
sections.summary: Despite increased urbanisation and more variable weather, flood-prone areas have been reduced from 3,200 hectares in the 1970s to 30.5 hectares today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Despite increased urbanisation and more variable weather, flood-prone areas have been reduced from 3,200 hectares in the 1970s to 30.5 hectares today.

sections.label: Paya Lebar flood cause and upgrading
sections.summary: The Paya Lebar flood on 24 December 2016 was caused by intense rain overwhelming the upstream Geylang River, and drainage upgrading works are expected to be completed in the third-quarter of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For the Paya Lebar flood on 24 December 2016, it was caused by intense rain which overwhelmed the upstream section of the Geylang River, thereby causing low-lying areas to flood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The expected completion of the drainage upgrading works is in the third-quarter of 2018.

sections.label: Upper Thomson Road flash flood cause
sections.summary: The flash flood at Upper Thomson Road on 24 December 2016 was due to localised constriction at a temporary diversion drain built by contractor Sato Kogyo, affecting the public drainage system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The flash flood at Upper Thomson Road on 24 December 2016 was due to localised constriction at a temporary diversion drain built by the contractor, Sato Kogyo, and this affected the public drainage system.
